arxiv-2205-12701.title: Eliciting and Understanding Cross-Task Skills with Task-Level Mixture-of-Experts
arxiv-2205-12701.creator: Qinyuan Ye, Juan Zha, Xiang Ren
arxiv-2205-12701.description: Abstract Recent works suggest that transformer models are capable of multi-tasking on diverse NLP tasks and adapting to new tasks efficiently. However, the potential of these multi-task models may be limited as they use the same set of parameters for all tasks.

arxiv-2301-13404.title: Opaque Contracts
arxiv-2301-13404.creator: Andreas Haupt, Zoë Hitzig
arxiv-2301-13404.description: Abstract Firms have access to abundant data on market participants. They use these data to target contracts to agents with specific characteristics, and describe these contracts in opaque terms. In response to such practices, recent proposed regulations aim to increase transparency, especially in digital markets.

arxiv-2404-03270.title: Riemannian L-systems: Modeling growing forms in curved spaces
arxiv-2404-03270.creator: Christophe Godin, Frédéric Boudon
arxiv-2404-03270.description: Abstract In the past 50 years, the formalism of L-systems has been successfully used and developed to model the growth of filamentous and branching biological forms. These simulations take place in classical 2-D or 3-D Euclidean spaces. However, various biological forms actually grow in curved, non-Euclidean, spaces.

arxiv-2409-10352.title: Partial Ordering Bayesian Logistic Regression Model for Phase I Combination Trials and Computationally Efficient Approach to Operational Prior Specification
arxiv-2409-10352.creator: Weishi Chen
arxiv-2409-10352.description: Abstract Abstract Recent years have seen increased interest in combining drug agents and/or schedules. Several methods for Phase I combination-escalation trials are proposed, among which, the partial ordering continual reassessment method (POCRM) gained great attention for its simplicity and good operational characteristics.

arxiv-2411-15402.title: Scale-invariant total decay width Γ ⁡ ( H → b ​ b ¯ ) \Gamma(H\to b\bar{b}) using the novel method of characteristic operator
arxiv-2411-15402.creator: Jiang Yan, Xing-Gang Wu, Jian-Ming Shen, Xu-Dong Huang, Zhi-Fei Wu
arxiv-2411-15402.description: Abstract According to the renormalization group invariance, any physical observable should be invariant under different renormalization schemes and scales. Nevertheless, a fixed-order pQCD approximant cannot inherently satisfy this requirement, giving rise to the conventional scheme-and-scale ambiguities. The principle of maximum conformality (PMC) offers a process-independent approach to address these two types of ambiguities.

arxiv-2412-11636.title: Science Filter Characterization of the Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT) on board Aditya-L1.
arxiv-2412-11636.creator: Janmejoy Sarkar, Rushikesh Deogaonkar, Ravi Kesharwani, Sreejith Padinhatteeri, A. N. Ramaprakash, Durgesh Tripathi, Soumya Roy, Gazi A. Ahmed, Rwitika Chatterjee, Avyarthana Ghosh, Sankarasubramanian K, Aafaque Khan, Nidhi Mehandiratta, Netra Pillai, Swapnil Singh
arxiv-2412-11636.description: Abstract The Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope ( SUIT ) on board the Aditya-L1 mission is designed to observe the Sun across 200–400 nm wavelength. The telescope used 16 dichroic filters tuned at specific wavelengths in various combinations to achieve its science goals.

arxiv-2501-14090.title: Making Reliable and Flexible Decisions in Long-tailed Classification
arxiv-2501-14090.creator: Bolian Li li4468@purdue.edu
arxiv-2501-14090.description: Abstract Long-tailed classification is challenging due to its heavy imbalance in class probabilities. While existing methods often focus on overall accuracy or accuracy for tail classes, they overlook a critical aspect: certain types of errors can carry greater risks than others in real-world long-tailed problems.

arxiv-2505-02750.title: A CRISP approach to QSP: XAI enabling fit-for-purpose models
arxiv-2505-02750.creator: Noah DeTal
arxiv-2505-02750.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Noah DeTal. Abstract

Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP) promises to accelerate drug development, enable personalized medicine, and improve the predictability of clinical outcomes. Realizing this potential requires effectively managing the complexity of mathematical models representing biological systems. Here, we present and validate a novel QSP workflow–CRISP (Contextualized Reduction for Identifiability and Scientific Precision)–that addresses a central challenge in QSP: the problem of complexity and over-parameterization, in which models contain irrelevant parameters that obscure interpretation and hinder predictive reliability.

britannica-1911-fez.title: Fez (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-fez.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-fez.description: Article 'Fez' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was incorporated in 1548. It lies in 34° 6′ 3″ N., 4° 38′ 15″ W., about 230 m. from the Atlantic and 85 m. of the Mediterranean. It is beautifully situated in a deep valley on the Wad Fās, an affluent of the Wad Sebu, which divides the town into two parts—the ancient town, Fās el Bali, on the right bank, and the new, Fās el Jadīd, on the left.

pmc-10496302.creator: Maryam Rafiee, Ezzat Allah Ghaemi
pmc-10496302.description: ObjectiveThe purpose of the present study was to investigate the biofilm production, and the presence of virulence genes and biochemical characteristics among the S. saprophyticus clinical isolates. A total of 35 clinical isolates of S. saprophyticus were collected from patients referred to several hospitals. By the crystal violet staining method, the capability of biofilm formation was performed.

pmc-10617736.title: National debt management and business sustainability in Africa’s largest economy: A focus on the private sector
pmc-10617736.creator: Mengya Shang, Uchechukwu E. Okorie, Yin Hang, Xiaosong Jin, Daniel E. Ufua, Magdalena Radulescu, Magdalena Radulescu, Magdalena Radulescu
pmc-10617736.description: In many developing economies, high and increasing public debt profile constitutes an essential means of financial risk. An appropriate debt management is germane for survival of business and good international reputation though its effect on private sector credit mobilization had been seldomly investigated.

pmc-11414143.title: SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence and preeclampsia markers in Mozambican pregnant women with perinatal loss
pmc-11414143.creator: Maureen Chileshe, Tacilta Nhampossa, Carla Carrilho, Anete Mendes, Elvira Luis, Jahit Sacarlal, Jessica Navero-Castillejos, Manuel Morales-Ruiz, Miguel J. Martínez, Jaume Ordi, Natalia Rakislova, Clara Menendez, Raquel González
pmc-11414143.description: BackgroundSARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy is known to be associated with poor pregnancy outcomes, including pre-eclampsia (PE), prematurity, perinatal and maternal mortality. Data on the burden of SARS-CoV-2 infection among pregnant women and their offspring in Sub-Saharan Africa is limited. We aimed to estimate SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence and determine PE biomarkers in Mozambican pregnant women with perinatal loss.

pmc-11529391.title: Superior Capsular Reconstruction for Massive Rotator Cuff Tear
pmc-11529391.creator: Sumpada Priambudi
pmc-11529391.description: Massive rotator cuff tears (RCT) defined as defects measuring >5 cm or involving two or more torn tendons. Irreparable RCT are generally large and retracted with poor or attenuated tissue quality, muscular atrophy, and fatty infiltration. Surgical options for irreparable RCT are arthroscopic debridement, partial repair, margin convergence, patch graft, tendon transfer, balloon spacer, and reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (RSA).

pmc-11599055.title: Feline Hemotropic Mycoplasma Species of Apparently Healthy Domestic Cats in Konya Province of Türkiye
pmc-11599055.creator: Ceylan Ceylan, Muhammed Hudai Culha, Gonca Sonmez, Muhammed Ahmed Selcuk, Merve Ider, Ayşe Evci, Sule Yılmaz, Ferda Sevinc, Onur Ceylan, Valentina Virginia Ebani
pmc-11599055.description: Simple SummaryThis study investigated the presence of hemotropic Mycoplasma species, which cause an emerging disease in domestic cats, in Konya province, Türkiye. We tested 384 apparently healthy cats and found that 9.4% of them were infected with Mycoplasma species, including Mycoplasma hemofelis, Mycoplasma hemocanis, Candidatus Mycoplasma turicensis, and Candidatus Mycoplasma hemominutum.

pmc-12563189.title: Microbial and Chemical Water Quality Assessments Across the Rural and Urban Areas of Nepal: A Scoping Review
pmc-12563189.creator: Suhana Chattopadhyay, Alex Choiniere, Nedelina Tchangalova, Yunika Acharya, Amy R Sapkota, Leena Malayil, Jun Hou
pmc-12563189.description: Nepal is currently facing critical water quality challenges due to urbanization, water management and governance issues, as well as natural disasters. This has resulted in the presence of harmful contaminants (e.g., pathogens, nitrates, arsenic) across multiple water sources, subsequently leading to waterborne disease risks (e.g., cholera and typhoid).

pmc-12581417.title: Long-term waist circumference and diabetes risk in premenopausal women: role of shared risk factors
pmc-12581417.creator: Hye Ah Lee
pmc-12581417.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe menopausal transition, a critical period for midlife women’s health, is marked by visceral fat redistribution. Although obesity and diabetes share common risk factors, their independent contributions to health risk remain unclear. This study investigated the association between 10-year mean waist circumference (WC) and incident type 2 diabetes in premenopausal women, and evaluated the impact of shared risk factors on both measures.MethodsUsing data from a community-based cohort with 16 years of follow-up, 1,482 premenopausal women at baseline were analyzed.

pmc-12703426.title: Bio‐Based Fluorescent Epoxies: Emission Control through Molecular Packing and Phase Separation
pmc-12703426.creator: Siddhant Bhardwaj, Andrew Becker, Dhananjay Dileep, Demetrius Finley, Jared Kaczor, Samuel Chambers, Gautham Pullela, Violet Krider, Michael Forrester, George Kraus, Eric W. Cochran
pmc-12703426.description: This study demonstrates the sustainable conversion of agricultural waste into high‐performance fluorescent epoxy resins through direct blending of coumaric acid epoxy (CE) and ferulic acid epoxy (FE) derived from corn stover. These bio‐based resins exhibit tunable photoluminescence, with emission maxima shifting from 299 nm to 841 nm as FE content increases from 0 to 33 wt%.

pmc-12987002.title: Soft Optical Sensor for Embryo Quality Evaluation Based on Multi-Focal Image Fusion and RAG-Enhanced Vision Transformers
pmc-12987002.creator: Domas Jonaitis, Vidas Raudonis, Egle Drejeriene, Agne Kozlovskaja-Gumbriene, Andres Salumets
pmc-12987002.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Multi-focal image fusion increases embryo classification accuracy by 9.43% compared to standard single-plane microscopy, effectively recovering lost morphological details.The proposed Swin-Transformer Soft Sensor achieves 94.11% diagnostic accuracy on a large-scale clinical dataset (N = 102,308). What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13255074.title: Iron-sulfur cofactors in nucleic acid metabolism and protein synthesis: Assembly, delivery, and putative roles in cellular and viral systems
pmc-13255074.creator: Nunziata Maio, Tracey A Rouault
pmc-13255074.description: Composed of iron (Fe) and inorganic sulfur (S), iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) are ancient cofactors present across all domains of life and in some viruses. Over the past 3 decades, cytosolic and nuclear Fe-S proteins have emerged as integral components of DNA replication and repair machineries, telomere maintenance pathways, transcriptional processes, cell cycle regulation, and protein synthesis.

pmc-13285570.title: Voices From the Outbreak: Exploring the Role of Migration, Literacy, and Healthcare Accessibility in Immunization Coverage of Banda District in the Bundelkhand Region of Uttar Pradesh, India
pmc-13285570.creator: Lal Divakar Singh, Mohd Maroof, Suneel Kumar Kaushal, Shailendra Singh Chaudhary, Jalaj Chaturvedi
pmc-13285570.description: Background: During August-September 2024, a diphtheria outbreak involving 10 children was reported from Devkher village of Naraini Block, Banda district, Uttar Pradesh, India. Despite the availability of diphtheria-containing vaccines under India's Universal Immunization Program, immunization gaps continue to persist in underserved rural communities.

pmc-13326471.title: Body mass index, physical activity, and epigenetic aging: a cross-population study
pmc-13326471.creator: Bojun Zhou, Dongzhe Wu, Shuting Chen, Shiyan Zhang, Xiaochuan Ge, Jiaming Li, Lianghao Zhu, Shijie Zhou, Ninghao Chang, Biao Zhou, Lei Zhang, Hua Meng
pmc-13326471.description: BackgroundObservational studies have suggested that body mass index (BMI) is associated with accelerated epigenetic aging; however, the age at which this association begins and the duration of its effects have not been fully established. This study evaluated the effects of BMI and physical activity on epigenetic aging from early life to adulthood.

pmc-13327627.creator: Hui Li, Xuanyu Tao, Lina Sun, Aifen Zhou, Jizhong Zhou

pmc-13377110.title: Comparing feedback learning and arousal responses in Down, Fragile X, and Williams syndromes
pmc-13377110.creator: Astrid E. Z. Hallman, Charlotte Willfors, Matilda A. Frick, Ann Nordgren, Johan Lundin Kleberg
pmc-13377110.description: Mechanisms underlying feedback learning in intellectual disability (ID) remain poorly understood. Down syndrome (DS), Fragile X syndrome (FXS), and Williams syndrome (WS) are genetic syndromes associated with ID, with distinct attention and arousal regulation profiles. Pupil dilation is a well-established index of feedback processing in typical development; little is known about these processes in non-social learning in these syndromes.

pmc-13403769.title: Vaccination as a Treatment for Patients With CVD
pmc-13403769.creator: Paul Allen Heidenreich
pmc-13403769.description: underutilized preventive strategies in cardiovascular medicine. Despite mounting evidence that vaccines can reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, vaccination rates among cardiac patients remain suboptimal. Cardiologists and other cardiology clinicians are uniquely positioned to address this gap, serving as trusted advisors who can both recommend and facilitate vaccination for their high-risk patients.1 The evidence for vaccination initially was observational.
